notes: §1985:VI.5.3.4 GR2 requires "Each condition-name requires a separate entry with level-number 88", that the entries "must immediately follow the entry describing the item with which the condition-name is associated", and that the item is none of: another condition-name, "A level 66 item", "A group containing items with descriptions including JUSTIFIED, SYNCHRONIZED, or USAGE (other than USAGE IS DISPLAY)", "An index data item". DataBinder.BindEntries associates each level-88 entry with the entry it follows (a run of 88s shares one conditional variable) and records the pair; CheckConditionNameAssociationsPass.Run refuses an 88 that follows no data item (COBOL1977) and one whose variable matches a row of Sr24Exclusions (COBOL1976): rows a, b, c with d, and e are the four 1985 exclusions, searched to every depth of the group, and the remaining rows name 2002-and-later features no 1985 source can write. No edition arm is needed for those; the 1985 arm is the format: LevelNumberPass.CheckEntryFormat refuses an 88 that carries another clause, no VALUE or no name (COBOL1747), and the 2002 additions to format 3 (WHEN SET TO FALSE, IN alphabet-name, the VALID/INVALID format) are refused at --std 85 with COBOL0900 (probed). The witness tests a condition-name on a group of DISPLAY items before and after a MOVE (RenderCondition88); 20 probes covered each exclusion (COMP, BINARY group usage, PACKED-DECIMAL, INDEX, JUSTIFIED, SYNCHRONIZED members, a nested member, a level 66, an index item, a leading 88) and the legal cases (elementary COMP and JUSTIFIED variables, level 77, a list with THRU).

next.reason: 1985: 'Format 3 is used for each condition-name'; separate level-88 entry; entries immediately follow the conditional variable; association allowed except another condition-name, a level 66 item, a group containing JUSTIFIED/SYNCHRONIZED/non-DISPLAY items, an index data item. §2023:13.16.3 SR24 keeps all of that ('Each condition-name requires a separate entry with level-number 88', 'shall immediately follow', exclusions a) to e)) but opens with 'Format 3 or 4 is used for each condition-name': a level-88 entry may now take the validation format, which by §2023:13.16.4 GR4 'has the same meaning as in Format 3'. §2023:13.16.4 GR3 restates that Format 3 'contains the name of the condition and the value, values, or range of values'. The added exclusions (message-tag, object, pointer, ANY LENGTH, STRONG, variable-length group) touch only 2023 features. Looser through the added format; no exception condition.
